claims.scope: Exact STM32C542RCT6 source-only CoreSight transport, topology, DWT, ITM, BPU, ETM, TPIU and CTI. No debug connection, memory access, authentication, reset, trace capture or executable profile is authorized. DBGMCU freeze/low-power details and CPU/NVIC/MPU semantics remain separately owned candidates.

chapter_audit.qualification: Full extracted RM49.1 through49.11 read, including CTI map continuation on2539; this is not full architecture, register-field, protocol, debugger implementation or hardware qualification. Figure/bit-cell visual reconciliation remains open. Referenced Arm architecture/TRM documents were not available in this bounded pinned-source review.

contracts.detail: JTAG and SWD are mutually exclusive shared-pin interfaces. RM documents JTAG default after system or power-on reset, debug pins configured by hardware, and SWD protocol version2. DP and AP register offsets are transport addresses, explicitly not CPU-memory-bus addresses. Reading DRW or banked data triggers a target-bus transaction; RDBUFF can retrieve a prior result without starting another AP transaction. No automatic discovery reads or writes are admitted.

SWJ-DP reset is documented for power-on and Standby wake. Host JTCK/SWCLK must keep toggling for several cycles after access. DCLK is a gated system clock requested by CDBGPWRUPREQ and acknowledged separately; RM says it must be disabled on debugger disconnect. Processor debug/trace use processor clock. TPIU non-ID access requires DEMCR.TRCENA to avoid documented lockup. These prerequisites do not establish a complete connection or teardown algorithm.

Ordinary clock/power loss makes debug components inaccessible. Debug low-power emulation maintains clocks/power and changes normal behavior. It is not valid evidence of normal Stop/Standby power or retention. Existing DBGMCU candidate owns freeze controls and mode behavior.

RM links OPEN to RDP0 and CLOSED to RDP2/L2_wBS, with disabled debugger access while booting system flash. CLOSED CPU authentication table is internally inconsistent and not an access authorization rule. OEMKEY validation/regression and BSKEY transitions are source facts only; full RDP regression erases entire user flash. No credentials, password provisioning, validation, transitions or recovery operations are authorized.

AP0 is system APB debug access to DBGMCU/system ROM; SIZE=2 word only, TAR bits1:0 fixed zero, ADDRINC0/1. AP1 is AHB access with SIZE0/1/2 byte/halfword/word and ADDRINC0/1/2, including packed four-byte or two-halfword transfers. Banked data access is word only and does not auto-increment. Physical endpoint access restrictions and side effects still apply; AP capability does not authorize arbitrary reads, packed peripheral access or writes.

System, MCU and processor ROM tables are distinct. DBGMCU has AP0 alias0xE00E4000 and CPU alias0x44024000. ROM entries contain offsets and present/format bits rather than ordinary peripheral addresses; reserved entries ending2 are not admitted components. JTAG IDCODE0x6BA00477 and DP_DPIDR0x6BA02477 are distinct documented identities, not contradictory values. Target part0x44F0 and device family0x44F do not establish order code, package, board population or physical revision.

RM documents four comparators, a32-bit processor cycle counter, five8-bit profiling counters, PC sample register, watchpoint/trace/ETM events. Comparator0 alone has cycle matching; detailed capability IDs differ by slot. MATCH numeric encodings are delegated to unavailable Arm reference and remain unqualified. MATCHED means a match since last function-register read, so such reads can consume historical observation. POSTINIT writes are ignored while POSTCNT enabled; CYCEVTENA/PCSAMPLENA must be disabled as applicable before configuration. No calibrated timebase or lossless profiling guarantee follows.

ITM has32 stimulus ports; a write generates a trace packet whereas a read reports state, not prior stimulus data. FIFO_READY is bit0; DISABLE is bit1. TPR groups eight ports per privilege bit. Software, DWT and timestamp packets share arbitration and FIFO, with software highest priority. Timestamp is21-bit and prescaled1/4/16/64. TRACEBUSID must be nonzero and unique for multiple sources; ITM BUSY is not receiver confirmation. STALLENA can stall CPU to preserve hardware trace instead of dropping packets, affecting execution.

Eight instruction-address comparators at0x008+4*n, n0..7, with address bits31:1 and enable bit0. Global enable changes require KEY=1 or write is ignored. These are shared debugger resources, not eight application-owned breakpoints; a candidate must reserve slots and coordinate halt/monitor effects rather than assuming a write is passive.

RM explicitly configures ETM instruction trace only: data values/addresses, contextID, VMID, address comparator pairs, data comparators and sequencer states are not implemented in the listed ID registers. Four DWT comparator inputs, four external inputs, one reduced-function counter, one single-shot control and two resource-selection pairs are reported. Two events and two-entry return stack are documented. Generic selector field width does not admit nonexistent resources; unavailable Arm ETM programming/decoder details remain gates.

EN, IDLE and PMSTABLE are different observations; unknown reset values are not readiness. TRACEID must be unique and1..0x6F;0 and0x70..0x7F reserved. Synchronization period fixed1024bytes; cycle threshold12-bit with minimum4. Stalling changes CPU timing and does not prove overflow impossible. STICKYPD tracks power removal since last PDSR read. Claim SET reads indicate four supported bits, while claim CLR reads return current tag; tags alone are not an atomic ownership protocol. Full safe configuration/drain/release sequence remains unqualified.

TPIU accepts ETM/ITM, advertises parallel widths1..4 and asynchronous Manchester/NRZ. CSPSR must be one-hot and supported. SWO baud is TRACECLKIN/(PRESCALER+1), with13-bit prescaler; actual clock rate and electrical/receiver tolerances remain separate gates. In SWO with continuous formatter disabled, only ITM/DWT is output and ETM is discarded. Flush request/completion, upstream ITM BUSY/ETM IDLE and receiver delivery are distinct. TPIU4-byte FIFO and asynchronous clock relationship are documented, not a lossless-bandwidth guarantee.

CTI has four channels, eight trigger input/output slots, no external multiplexers. Tables name only input/output0..5;6/7 unused in those tables, with output-number conflict against figure retained. INEN/OUTEN map channel masks; INTACK acknowledges/clears outputs; APPPULSE self-clears; APPSET/APPCLEAR are persistent event control with source typo retained. EDBGRQ can halt CPU and DBGRESTART restart it. GATE propagation text does not establish another implemented CTI. No routing/start/halt/restart actions admitted.

Thirteen literal DEBUG package records are copied unchanged and hash-linked. PA13/PA14 SWD/JTAG aliases share the same pads, PB3 SWO/JTDO share a pad and SWO is documented only with SWD, and all trace/debug alternatives require common pin ownership with other consumers. Parallel trace pads PE2/PC1/PC8/PD2/PC12 are bonded on LQFP64. GPIO AF, DBGMCU TRACE_IOEN/TRACE_EN/mode, TPIU, upstream sources and receiver are separate gates; no board path/population or electrical qualification is inferred.

ES0676 applies to C542 and revisionsZ/Y; die identity is not observed. ES2.7.1 may repeatedly set RTC alarm flags during debug halt even with RTC freeze if nonzero MASKSS and alarm condition met just before halt/printf; no workaround is listed. ES2.1.1 MPU fault ordering remains owned CPU scope. Exact header has no SAU regions and RM says always nonsecure; generic CMSIS secure aliases do not establish exact secure functionality. No absence-of-CoreSight-specific-row immunity is claimed. ES core revision wording r0p1 and header r0p4_p1 are retained without choosing physical revision.

conflicts.detail: Table572 says CLOSED dbgen=1/spiden=1/niden=0/spniden=0 while description says debug and trace disabled and prose defines dbgen=1 enabled. DAP table separately has CLOSED dbgen=0. Preserve CPU/DAP distinction and inconsistency; do not infer usable closed-state access.

Table577 prints000 FAULT/010 WAIT/100 OK while nearby protocol says LSB-first. No pinned Arm ADI specification was reviewed to normalize encoding or bit order. Retain literal table; do not generate a protocol implementation from it.
DP_SELECTR detail/map use APSEL[7:0]; AP access prose2431/2432 says[3:0]. Only AP0/1 are documented valid, so do not expand based on either field width.

Table581 lists CFGR atF4 while Table582 reserves20..F4; AP1 CSWR detail reserves22:8 while map labels MODE[3:0]; map continuation repeats AP0_IDR for the AP1-valued row. RM2432 prose says TAR[31:4]+n but Table581 and2435 detail specify4*n. Preserve these discrepancies; no inferred arbitrary AP-register or transfer address access.

Intro2455 says data comparator COMP1 only; detailed FUNCTR1 capability list omits data-value while FUNCTR3 includes data-value and linked-data-value. Record per-source lists; no data-match executable domain admitted.
RM detail/map use0xFC8 while CMSIS DWT_Type DEVARCH offset is0xFBC. Neither is silently selected as a readable hardware address.

RM marks DWT CYCCNT and COMP r, ITM_TPR r and TPIU_CSPSR r, while surrounding programming prose and CMSIS declarations use writable fields. Read/write access markers alone do not admit automatic writes or polling. Exact access policy remains unresolved.

Table590 lists stimulus0..31 through07C but also starts reserved range at07C. It labels DEVARCH ARCHPART[3:0] versus detail11:0. Generic CMSIS defines GTSFREQ bits11:10 although RM reserves15:10; integration registers are also excluded by RM reserved span. Preserve conflicts rather than granting generic feature support.

DS33 broadly describes instruction and data flow, while RM2488 and ID registers explicitly exclude data tracing. Preserve source scope difference; do not admit ETM data-address/value trace from DS prose.

ETM_VICTLR describes EXLEVEL_S secure state despite RM always-nonsecure statement; do not infer secure trace. IDR0 reset0x280006E1 sets bits27 and0 described reserved; IDR1 reset0x4100F421 sets bits15:12 described reserved. Raw resets remain source literals, not synthesized writable initialization images or observed silicon values.
CSPSR may only be modified with formatter stopped, but FFSR.FTNONSTOP is1 (cannot stop) and FTSTOPPED described0. No safe width-reconfiguration sequence is established from these pages.

RM fieldPSCOUNT[12:0] is13bits, prose calls it12-bit with maximum4096 and default64frames/1024bytes, while reset is0. CMSIS mask0x1F is5bits. Do not resolve encoded period/default or derive executable bounds from these conflicting descriptions.
TPIU advertises1..4 widths including3; DBGMCU trace pin modes name1,2,4 only. Three-bit physical routing/configuration combination is unqualified; no claim that it works or is impossible.
Figure749 labels ETMEXTIN0..3 as TRIGOUT4..7; Table595 maps them to outputs2..5 and marks6/7 unused. Preserve both mappings and block concrete CTI event routes until reconciled.

APPSET channel0 active/set entries repeatXXX0 instead of a distinct active value. CTI_PIDR0 detail/reset2535 gives0x21 but map2539 reset binary00010001 gives0x11. Keep literal disagreement; do not derive an action write or identity from a chosen correction.

source_derived_SDK_gates.detail: CMSIS ITM_SendChar checks only ITMENA and port0 TER, waits indefinitely while the entire u32 stimulus read equals zero, writes low8bits of ch, and always returns original ch. It does not test FIFO_READY bit0 specifically, timeout, TRCENA, authentication, GPIO/TPIU or receiver state. If disable state changes after the initial check, a nonzero DISABLE status can end the equality wait without FIFO_READY. This is a conditional source-level gap, not an observed loss/hang. Caller ownership, bounded waits, status-mask validation and teardown/race control remain required.

ITM_ReceiveChar and ITM_CheckChar access external volatile ITM_RxBuffer, not hardware SWO input. Receive reads then clears sentinel in separate operations; concurrent producer/consumer synchronization is not implemented. No actual hardware receive path or loss-free mailbox is established. DIB_GetAuthStatus is a bare register read, not a policy/enforcement or device identity check. Secure getter is conditional generic code.

CMSIS exposes generic DCB/DIB, ITM integration registers, TPIU integration registers and security-related masks. RM reserves ITM E84..FB8 except named DEVARCH and TPIU30C..F9C, excluding the CMSIS integration offsets. Those generic symbols are not admitted exact features. Bare volatile structures provide no locking, ownership, state or range enforcement. DCB halt/step/register-transfer and debug monitor fields are recorded as source names only; complete Arm sequencing and sticky-read semantics are outside locally pinned evidence.

finite_source_maps.qualification: Literal bounded source maps; not executable register schemas or access admission. Reserved fields, unknown resets and conflicts require separate reconciliation.

open_gates: All conflicting offsets, encodings, access markers and identities must be reconciled before executable imports; no automatic reads, writes or register polling are authorized.

Every physical pin, trace source ID, comparator, CTI channel and shared control register requires coherent ownership with debugger/firmware; claim registers alone are insufficient.
Trace delivery, bandwidth, stalls, overflow/loss, receiver configuration, timing and electrical operation remain untested.
No actual identity/revision, security state, connection, build or target behavior was observed; low-power/freeze source contracts remain separate.
